title: Telling stories & real conversation
goal: Tell a story with natural connectors, describe people and things with relative clauses, report what others said, and use everyday fillers and proverbs.
intro:
Nepalis love a good **गफ** (chat) over tea, and a good story. In this final unit you'll learn the tools that make Nepali sound fluent: the linking form **-एर** ('having done'), **-दा** ('while/when'), the 'surprise' ending **रहेछ** ('it turned out…'), the hearsay particle **रे** ('apparently'), relative clauses built from participles (हिजो आएको मान्छे 'the man who came yesterday'), and reported speech with **भनेर**.

You'll also pick up the fillers and proverbs that pepper everyday conversation. बधाई छ — you've reached the end of the course!

vocab.note: गफ गर्नु 'to chat'. गफ नदे! 'don't talk nonsense!'
जति … उति 'the more … the more'; दस जति 'about ten'.
ऊ आउँछ रे 'apparently he's coming'. के रे? 'what did they say?'
Marks a discovery: यो त मिठो रहेछ! 'oh, this is tasty!'
खै, थाहा छैन 'dunno'. खै मेरो चाबी? 'now where's my key?'

vocab.en: (particle) you know; what about…?; of course
vocab.note: हो नि 'of course'; तपाईं नि? 'and you?'
Softens and seeks agreement: जाऊँ है 'I'll go, OK?'
मतलब के हो? 'what does it mean?'

vocab.en: to tell, recount; to let hear

phrases.en: What did they say? / What was that?
Oh, so he's actually a doctor!
I mean, what I'm trying to say is…
A bad dancer blames the crooked courtyard.
phrases.note: Proverb: a bad workman blames his tools.

phrases.en: You can't clap with one hand.
phrases.note: It takes two (to quarrel / to cooperate).

phrases.en: As the country, so the dress.
phrases.note: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.

phrases.en: Which is bigger, brains or the buffalo?

grammar.title: Storytelling tools: -एर, -दा, रहेछ
grammar.body:
**-एर** 'having done, and then' links actions in sequence without needing 'and': घर **गएर** खाना खाएँ 'I went home and ate'. Vowel stems: खाएर, आएर; irregular: गएर (जानु), भएर (हुनु). It also expresses manner: हिँडेर 'on foot', बसेर 'sitting'.

**-दा** 'while / when (doing)': बाटोमा **हिँड्दा** 'while walking along the road', सानो **हुँदा** 'when (I was) small', घर **पुग्दा** 'by the time I got home'. Vowel stems: खाँदा, जाँदा.

**रहेछ / -एछ** — the **mirative**, Nepali's 'surprise' form. It marks something you've just discovered or realised: यो त मिठो **रहेछ**! 'Oh, this is tasty!' (I didn't expect it). In the past: राति पानी **परेछ** 'it rained last night (I see from the puddles)'; ऊ त गइसकेको **रहेछ** 'turns out he had already left'. It's the punchline form of Nepali storytelling.

Connectors: पहिले/सुरुमा 'first', अनि/त्यसपछि 'then', अचानक 'suddenly', तर 'but', बल्ल 'finally', अन्तमा 'in the end'.

examples.en: I get up in the morning and have tea.
When I was small I used to live in the village.

examples.native: बजार जाँदा मैले पुरानो साथी भेटेँ।
examples.roman: bajār jāṃdā maile purāno sāthi bheṭeṃ.
examples.en: On my way to the market I met an old friend.

examples.native: ओहो, आज त बिदा पो रहेछ!
examples.roman: oho, āja ta bidā po rahechha!
examples.en: Oh, it turns out today's a holiday!
When I opened the door and looked, there was nobody.

grammar.title: Relative clauses: participles and जुन/जो
grammar.body:
Nepali usually makes relative clauses with **participles placed before the noun** — no 'who/which' needed:

**-एको** (completed): हिजो **आएको** मान्छे 'the man who came yesterday', मैले **किनेको** किताब 'the book (that) I bought'.
**-ने** (habitual/future): नेपाली **बोल्ने** मान्छे 'people who speak Nepali', भोलि **जाने** बस 'the bus that leaves tomorrow', **बस्ने** ठाउँ 'a place to stay'.

There is also a **correlative** pattern with जो/जुन/जहाँ/जब answered by ऊ/त्यो/त्यहाँ/तब, common in careful speech and writing:
**जुन** किताब मैले किनेँ, **त्यो** राम्रो छ 'The book (which) I bought is good.'
**जहाँ** इच्छा, **त्यहाँ** उपाय 'Where there's a will, there's a way.'
**जसले** मेहनत गर्छ, **उसले** फल पाउँछ 'Whoever works hard gets the reward.'

examples.native: त्यो रातो ज्याकेट लगाएको केटी मेरी बहिनी हो।
examples.roman: tyo rāto jyākeṭ lagāeko keṭi meri bahini ho.
examples.en: That girl wearing the red jacket is my sister.

examples.native: तपाईंले पकाएको खाना एकदम मिठो छ।
examples.roman: tapāiṃle pakāeko khānā ekdam miṭho chha.
examples.en: The food you cooked is really tasty.
Is there anyone here who speaks English?
The hotel where I'm staying is nearby.
Where there's a will, there's a way.

grammar.title: Reporting speech: भन्यो, भनेर, रे
grammar.body:
Nepali reports speech **directly**, keeping the original words (and their person), followed by **भन्यो/भनिन्/भन्नुभयो** 'said':
उसले "म भोलि आउँछु" **भन्यो** — 'He said he would come tomorrow' (lit. He said, "I'll come tomorrow").

**भनेर** (lit. 'having said') works like English 'that' after verbs of thinking, knowing, hearing and asking: ऊ आउँछ **भनेर** मलाई थाहा थियो 'I knew that he would come'. It also means 'so that / intending to': तपाईंलाई भेट्छु **भनेर** आएँ 'I came (in order) to see you'.

**रे** at the end of a sentence marks **hearsay** — 'apparently, they say, he says': भोलि बन्द छ **रे** 'apparently there's a strike tomorrow'. **के रे?** 'what did they say?'

Yes/no reported questions use **कि** 'whether': ऊ आउँछ **कि** आउँदैन, थाहा छैन 'I don't know whether he's coming or not'.

examples.en: Mum told me to come home quickly.

examples.native: उनले मलाई "तिमी कहाँ बस्छौ?" भनेर सोधिन्।
examples.roman: unle malāi "timi kahāṃ baschhau?" bhanera sodhin.
examples.en: She asked me where I live.

examples.native: ऊ बिरामी छ भनेर मैले सुनेँ।
examples.roman: u birāmi chha bhanera maile suneṃ.

examples.native: बस आउँछ कि आउँदैन, कसैलाई थाहा छैन।
examples.roman: bas āuṃchha ki āuṃdaina, kasailāi thāhā chhaina.
examples.en: Nobody knows whether the bus is coming or not.

dialogue.title: The yeti of Lobuche
dialogue.setting: Around the stove in a teahouse, Pemba tells Tom a story from his early days as a trekking guide.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.en: Shall I tell you a story?

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: दस वर्ष अघि, म पहिलो पटक गाइड भएर एभरेस्टतिर गएको थिएँ।
lines.roman: das barsa aghi, ma pahilo paṭak gāiḍ bhaera Ebhresṭtira gaeko thieṃ.
lines.en: Ten years ago I went to the Everest region for the first time as a guide.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: एक रात हामी लोबुचेमा बसेका थियौँ। अचानक बाहिर ठूलो आवाज आयो।
lines.roman: ek rāt hāmi Lobuchemā baseka thiyauṃ. achānak bāhira ṭhulo āwāj āyo.
lines.en: One night we were staying at Lobuche. Suddenly there was a loud noise outside.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: सबै पाहुनाहरू "यती आयो! यती आयो!" भनेर कराउन थाले।
lines.roman: sabai pāhunāharu "yeti āyo! yeti āyo!" bhanera karāuna thāle.
lines.en: All the guests started shouting, "The yeti's here! The yeti's here!"

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: म टर्च लिएर बाहिर गएँ। हेर्दा त…
lines.roman: ma ṭarch liera bāhira gaeṃ. herdā ta…
lines.en: I took a torch and went outside. And when I looked…

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: भान्साबाट आलु चोरेर खाँदै गरेको एउटा याक पो रहेछ!
lines.roman: bhānsābāṭa ālu chorera khāṃdai gareko euṭā yāk po rahechha!
lines.en: …it turned out to be a yak that had stolen potatoes from the kitchen and was eating them!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: हाहा! हात्ती आयो, हात्ती आयो, फुस्सा!
lines.roman: hāhā! hātti āyo, hātti āyo, phussā!
lines.en: Haha! All that fuss for nothing!

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: हो नि! त्यसैदेखि साथीहरूले मलाई "यती गाइड" भन्छन्।
lines.roman: ho ni! tyasaidekhi sāthiharule malāi "yeti gāiḍ" bhanchhan.
lines.en: Exactly! Ever since then my friends have called me the 'Yeti Guide'.

culture: Conversation in Nepal is a social art. **गफ** over tea can last for hours, and stories are told with dramatic pauses, the punchline marked by **पो रहेछ!** Proverbs (**उखान टुक्का**) are used constantly, even by young people, and quoting one at the right moment wins instant approval. In the hills you may hear **दोहोरी**, a sung, improvised back-and-forth where a man and a woman trade witty verses. Young urban Nepalis mix in a lot of English ('*actually*, म *busy* छु यार'), but older people and villagers will be most delighted when you speak plain Nepali — and they will tell everyone about the विदेशी who spoke it. शुभकामना!
